name_en: Chisha namasu — crinkled lettuce tossed with vinegared miso and flaked fish
summary_ja: 下関の伝統野菜「かきちしゃ」をちぎり、酢みそやほぐした焼き魚、しらすであえる料理。関ヶ原の戦い後、困窮した毛利の人々が考案したと伝わり、「ちしゃもみ」の名でも親しまれている。
summary_en: Kakichisha, an heirloom crinkled lettuce grown around Shimonoseki, is torn by hand and tossed with vinegared miso, flaked grilled fish, or whitebait. It is said to have been devised by the Mori domain's people after being impoverished by the Battle of Sekigahara, and is also known as "chishamomi."
source_title: ちしゃなます 山口県

name_en: Fuku sashi — paper-thin pufferfish sashimi arranged in a chrysanthemum pattern
summary_ja: 透けるほど薄く切ったふぐの刺身を菊の花のように盛り付ける下関の一皿。福を呼ぶ意味で「ふぐ」を「ふく」と呼び、ポン酢と薬味で食す。明治21年、下関でのみふぐ食が解禁されたのが始まりと伝わる。
summary_en: Pufferfish sashimi is sliced so thin it becomes translucent, then arranged in a chrysanthemum pattern in this Shimonoseki dish. Locals call the fish "fuku," a homophone for good fortune, and eat it with citrus ponzu and scallion; the practice traces to 1888, when eating pufferfish was legalized in Yamaguchi alone.
